stem: A 9-year-old girl falls from a first-floor balcony and is brought to the emergency department with severe neck pain. Which clinical features are important to assess when deciding whether the cervical spine can be clinically cleared?
explanation: Cervical spine clearance after trauma relies on assessing for midline tenderness and other high-risk features such as altered consciousness, intoxication, focal neurological deficit, and distracting injury. In this rewritten single-best-answer item, midline cervical tenderness is the best answer because it is a key examination feature that prevents clinical clearance.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Trauma 2 - Pain

rationale: The original question was multiple-answer. To make it a single-best-answer item, it was rewritten to ask for one key clinical feature used in cervical spine assessment/clearance.

optionExplanations.A: Yes — midline cervical tenderness is a key sign of possible cervical spine injury.
optionExplanations.B: No — isolated limb bruising is not a standard cervical spine clearance feature.
optionExplanations.C: No — abdominal pain alone does not specifically assess cervical spine clearance.
optionExplanations.D: No — a minor scalp abrasion is not a major clearance criterion.
optionExplanations.E: No — normal observations do not by themselves clear the cervical spine.

Clinical scenario 3 - Anna

The following eight questions refer to Anna’s clinical scenario.

Teaching/learning points:

Immobilisation in children

Anatomical differences

SCIWORA

The triage nurse rushes into resuscitation with nine year old Anna and her parents. Anna is in her father’s arms. She has fallen from their first-floor balcony onto the lawn below. Her fall was not witnessed but heard by her parents, who immediately found her on her back in the garden crying. Rather than calling an ambulance, Anna’s parents brought her to emergency in their car.

The triage nurse is concerned Anna has fallen a significant height (greater than twice her standing height). Anna initially appears alert and very distressed. She is complaining of severe neck and back pain. Her respiratory rate is 26/min, saturations 100% in air, heart rate 110bpm, blood pressure 100/60. Based on her mechanism of injury, Anna was immediately secured on a spinal board with three straps, a hard cervical collar and sandbags.
